summary:
We developed Echoes of Dust, an interactive web-based storytelling and educational gaming platform for the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge. Built using official NASA data from PDS, NSSDC, Moon/Mars Trek, and the NASA Image and Video Library, the platform features a 3D topographic map of the Moon and Mars pinpointing six iconic decommissioned missions—including Opportunity, InSight, and the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle. Users explore first-person journals that personify these spacecraft, recounting their discoveries and final moments before losing contact, alongside a Mars terrain mini-game, science quizzes, and unlockable Explorer Badges.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming dense, technical archival data into an accessible, emotionally engaging experience for students. This is important because over 100 NASA explorers sit silently on the Moon and Mars, often overlooked beyond major landing milestones. By humanizing their journeys, Echoes of Dust inspires STEM curiosity and honors the robotic pioneers paving the way for Artemis and future Mars missions.

Here is a complete draft for your Project Details section based on your presentation:

What It Does & How It Works

Echoes of Dust is a browser-based interactive storytelling and educational gaming platform that brings NASA's decommissioned lunar and Martian spacecraft to life through three core features:

  • 3D Exploration Map: Users navigate interactive topographic maps of the Moon and Mars to locate the exact landing coordinates of six iconic missions (three on the Moon and three on Mars, including Opportunity, InSight, and the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle).
  • First-Person Spacecraft Journals: Clicking a mission opens a first-person narrative written from the spacecraft's perspective, pairing high-resolution NASA imagery with its discoveries, challenges, and final moments before losing contact (such as Opportunity's last transmission before the 2018 dust storm).
  • Mini-Game & Quizzes: Users play an interactive Mars terrain-navigation mini-game, answer science quizzes after each chapter to reinforce what they learned, and unlock collectible Explorer Badges for each spacecraft.

Our team built this through a three-step workflow: curating six historically significant missions, translating their technical parameters and decommissioning causes into accessible first-person scripts, and integrating the stories, NASA imagery, 3D maps, and mini-games into a single web platform.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Accessible STEM Learning: Turns dense, academic archival data into an intuitive experience tailored for school-aged students.
  • Inspiring the Next Generation: Sparks interest in science and space exploration by combining emotional storytelling with hands-on gameplay.
  • Honoring Space Pioneers: Highlights the legacy of the 100+ silent robotic explorers on the Moon and Mars that paved the way for human return missions like Artemis and future Mars exploration.
  • Scalability: Designed to expand toward deep-space probes (Voyager 1 & 2, Cassini, New Horizons), mobile Augmented Reality (AR) 3D models, and bilingual Vietnamese/English voiceovers for international students.

Tools, Data Sources & Software Used

  • NASA Data & Mapping Platforms: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDC), NASA Image and Video Library (images.nasa.gov), NASA Moon Trek & Mars Trek (trek.nasa.gov), and NASA Science – Solar System Exploration (science.nasa.gov).
  • Development: Browser-based web development and interactive mini-game programming. (Note: Your slides don't list the exact coding languages, frameworks, or hardware you used—add those here if you'd like judges to see your specific tech stack.)

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

  • Creative Approach: Instead of presenting static timelines or technical spec sheets, we personified the spacecraft—giving silent machines a voice to tell their own stories and say goodbye.
  • Student Accessibility: We stripped away intimidating technical jargon in favor of relatable storytelling and an easy-to-use browser interface that requires no downloads.
  • Scientific Accuracy: Every landing coordinate, operational timeline, image, and end-of-mission cause is grounded directly in official NASA datasets.
  • Engagement Balance: We paired emotional narratives with active mini-games and quizzes so students both connect with the missions and retain key scientific concepts.
